A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, methods, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including material reorganized between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy, logical-consistency, efficiency, prompting, and fine-tuning experiments, including additional evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised two-shot prompting results in Table 12.

M1.justification: The proposed KG-context retrieval, instruction-dataset construction, and QLoRA supervised fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2 and Sections 3–4. Additional prompt documentation and the CNF proposition do not establish a changed core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FreebaseLFC, NELLLFC, WikiLFC, FEVER, and the same four general-language benchmarks. De Morgan’s laws, first-order logic, and syllogism experiments already appear in v1; their dedicated treatment in v2 does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Gemma-2B, Llama2-7B/13B/70B, GPT-4o, MiniCheck-FT5, and the same prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning alternatives. Renaming few-shot prompting to two-shot prompting does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: The documented two-example prompt changes from repeated factual-correctness instructions in v1’s page-25 textbox to a system-prefaced Context/Question/Answer template in v2 Figure 5. Both use one positive and one negative example. This is a reported protocol revision, without establishing reruns; splits, training budgets, and evaluation-based checkpoint selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing prompting ablation is revised through the changed two-shot template and updated Table 12 evidence. The context, retrieval, learning-rate, epoch, higher-order-logic, and language-benchmark analyses otherwise remain; new discussion of existing generalization results is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain the timing uncertainty entries in Table 7 and error bars in the language-benchmark plots, relocated from v1 Figure 7 to v2 Figure 11. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 12 changes Llama2-7B few-shot/two-shot accuracy from 0.69 to 0.78 and logical consistency from 0.40 to 0.58. Because the displayed prompt also changes, these are revised results rather than an established same-setting gain. V1’s conflicting extra prompting summary in Table 9 is removed; other matched results, including the headline 14% consistency improvement, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 3 and its proof in Appendix C, explicitly deriving the consistency criterion for conjunctive normal form. This is a limited formal extension alongside the retained DNF proposition, correctness-to-consistency proposition, and their proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly incorporates first-order logic and syllogism into the stated assessment scope, drawing on experiments already present in v1. It also softens the claim that consistency permits direct verification to saying verification becomes easier. The three central contributions and headline fine-tuning claim remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix H discussion attributes high De Morgan consistency to always-true predictions and interprets the existing training-mixture comparisons. Appendix K.2 adds an explicit rationale for prompting closed-source models. Some new interpretations overstate the tables: H.1 concludes that consistency improves although Table 14 shows decreases from 1.00 to 0.98 and 0.99 to 0.95.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete code/benchmark repository link and release statement, replacing reliance on a generic supplementary-materials reference. It also supplies fuller simple-fact and CoT prompts and explains natural-language rendering of logical operators and quantifiers. These are documentation additions; the reported hardware and fine-tuning hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against earlier consistency, KG, hallucination, and fact-checking research remain unchanged. Bibliographic differences are capitalization and formatting corrections.

P1.justification: The appendix undergoes substantial structural reorganization: the former broad experimental appendix is divided into datasets, system settings, numbered analyses, and generalization sections, with later evaluations reordered. V2 adds an appendix roadmap, expands explanations, edits language throughout, and updates author/header formatting and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 revises Figure 1, adds simple-fact, complex-fact, and CoT prompt displays, and redesigns the existing few-shot textbox as Figure 5. It separates De Morgan rows into Table 14, consolidates duplicate tables, and extensively relocates appendix displays. Existing experimental plots retain their underlying results.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility and readability through explicit access information, fuller prompt documentation, a CNF proof, and better-organized appendices with fewer duplicate displays. The core method and most evidence remain unchanged. New overgeneralizations in Appendix H and some stale cross-references temper these gains, but the documentation improvements support a limited positive overall assessment.
